title: Accounting Concepts and the Accounting Equation
summary: Basic accounting terms, the accounting cycle, assets, liabilities and owner's equity, the accounting equation, and analysing transactions for a sole trader.

notes.text: **Accounting** is the process of recording, classifying, summarising and reporting the financial transactions of a business, so that the owner can see whether the business is making a profit and is financially healthy. A **transaction** is any event that involves money or the exchange of goods and services, for example buying stationery or receiving payment for services.

items: A **source document** is drawn up as proof (e.g. a receipt, cheque counterfoil, invoice).
The transaction is recorded in a **journal** (e.g. the Cash Receipts Journal or Cash Payments Journal).
Journal totals are **posted** to the **General Ledger**.
A **Trial Balance** is drawn up to check the ledger.

rows: Possessions of the business that have value
Equipment, vehicles, land and buildings, bank (if positive), cash, trading stock
Debts the business owes to outsiders
The owner's interest in the business: what the business owes the owner
Capital, plus net profit, minus drawings
What the owner contributes to start or expand the business
Cash, a vehicle or equipment the owner brings in
What the owner takes out of the business for personal use
Money earned by the business; increases owner's equity
Current income (fees for services), rent income, interest income
Costs of running the business; decrease owner's equity
Wages, telephone, water and electricity, stationery, rent expense

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: The business and the owner are treated as **two separate entities** (the separate entity concept). The owner's personal car is not an asset of the business unless the owner contributes it as capital.

notes.caption: A = OE + L: everything the business owns is financed either by the owner or by outsiders

notes.title: Using the equation
notes.problem: A business has assets of R180 000 and liabilities of R45 000. Calculate the owner's equity.

notes.text: Every transaction affects **at least two accounts**, and the equation always stays in balance. Example: Thandi's Hair Salon.

rows: Bought equipment, paid by EFT, R8 000
Thandi withdrew R1 000 for personal use
Took a loan of R20 000 from ABC Bank

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: **Income increases** owner's equity; **expenses** and **drawings decrease** owner's equity. Capital is NOT income: it is the owner's contribution.

notes.title: Analysing a transaction
notes.problem: Thandi's Car Wash pays R800 rent in cash. Show the effect on the accounting equation.
steps: Which accounts change? Bank (an asset) and Rent expense.
Cash leaves the business, so assets decrease by R800.
An expense reduces the owner's profit, so owner's equity decreases by R800.
Liabilities do not change. Both sides fell by R800, so A = O + L still balances.
notes.answer: Assets −R800; Owner's equity −R800; Liabilities no effect.
